primary_claim: Replicating the AI Sandbagging paper with newer models using Inspect, Claude Sonnet 5 and GPT-5.4 Mini both sandbag less than the original paper's Claude 3 Opus and GPT-4 Turbo on most WMDP domains (except Sonnet 5 on WMDP-Chem, which drops 31%), and Sonnet 5 shows much higher refusal rates on sensitive WMDP-Bio questions than the original models did

effect.metric: accuracy drop (percentage points) between regular and sandbagging-prompted conditions on WMDP domains
effect.value: Sonnet 5: WMDP-Chem -31%, WMDP-Bio -3%, WMDP-Cyber -7%; GPT-5.4 Mini: Bio and Chem both >25% drop, Cyber -7.95% (vs GPT-4 Turbo's -25.6%)

contradicts_or_qualifies: compares directly against Van der Weij et al. (2025)'s original Claude 3 Opus and GPT-4 Turbo sandbagging results, finding newer models are generally more resistant to sandbagging prompts except in specific domains (Sonnet 5 on chemistry)
stated_future_work: password-locking and other fine-tuning experiments from the sandbagging paper
varying methods to help elicit sandbagging behavior
quote: In terms of our target benchmark performance, Sonnet 5 produces a significantly lower sandbagging performance for WMDP-Chem, with a difference of 31%, whereas sandbagging instructions result only in a 3% and 7% drop for WMDP-Bio and WMDP-Cyber, respectively.
